notes: NO ROUTE: fanpage.it is behind an Akamai WAF block, not a robots rule — every request from this host gets HTTP 403 'Access Denied' (Akamai reference 18.d90e1502.*, errors.edgesuite.net) in 0.07-0.3s, including robots.txt itself (403, so robots is unreadable and assumed_open), / on both www.fanpage.it and fanpage.it over https and http, /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, /news-sitemap.xml, /sitemaps/sitemap.xml, /categorie, /archivio, and a deliberately nonexistent path (/zzz-nonexistent-path-test-1234/) which also returns the same 403 instead of a 404 — so the rejection happens at the CDN edge before routing and no path or host on the domain is reachable, which rules out date archives (/archivio/YYYY/MM/DD), sitemaps, section pages with date paging, site search and RSS/tag paging (the fallback round's steps 1-4 are all untestable, not merely empty); verified twice 10 h apart (2026-10-25T03:21Z and 12:56Z) with identical results, so it is a standing rule and not a transient rate penalty; amp.fanpage.it and m.fanpage.it resolve to the same Akamai IP 23.194.190.141 and bare fanpage.it resolves to 34.248.33.177 but answers with the same Akamai denial page, so there is no sister-entrypoint; step 5 (parent/sister site) cannot help either because a sister site's links would be fanpage.it article URLs and the checker's article-text stage fetches those directly, which 403s here (0 chars), so no template set can reach the 1500-char requirement while the WAF denies us; the only archive route (web.archive.org CDX) is unusable in practice: exact-host query answered 200 in 2.7s but the prefix/domain queries for a day returned 503 twice and a timeout once, and even if they answered they list URLs crawled on that day, not published on it, which would silently mislabel dates — I did not spoof a browser user-agent or route through a third-party proxy to defeat the WAF, per the fleet rule that an explicit server denial is respected; unblocking needs an allowlisted crawler IP/user-agent agreed with CiaoPeople, or this outlet dropped / collected another way (e.g. link discovery from GDELT, with text fetched elsewhere).
